whyThisRecordExists.statement: Migration 0012 (transport-failure observability) advanced the repository's migration range from 0001..0011 to 0001..0012. FRAME_V2_GEN1 was materialised under 0001..0011 and stamps that range as provenance. The implementation record surfaced the divergence for owner awareness rather than amending it silently; this file is the owner's answer.

reasoning.aProvenanceStampRecordsTheConditionsOfMa: databaseSchemaVersion on a frozen frame says WHAT SCHEMA WAS IN PLACE WHEN THIS FRAME WAS MATERIALISED. It is not a claim about the present, and it does not become false when the schema advances - it would become false only if it were rewritten.
reasoning.whyBackfillingWouldBeTheError: Rewriting the stamp to 0001..0012 would assert that migration 0012 existed at A1 materialisation time. It did not. That is the same class of defect as back-filling an EWP snapshot's origin provenance (CLAUDE.md, 'an EWP snapshot records TWO different provenance facts') and the same class the append-only rules exist to prevent.
reasoning.whyTheFrameHashDivergenceIsNotADefect: The schema stamp is inside the hashed region, so re-materialising Gen-1 under this build would produce a different frameHash. That is the hash doing its job: it says 'these are different materialisations', which is TRUE. It does not say the membership changed, and the membership did not change.
reasoning.whatDidNotMove: No eligibility judgement, no organisation count, no draw, no split, no acquisition-of-record status.

forwardRule.whatSuchAnOutputWouldBe: A DIFFERENT PROSPECTIVE MATERIALISATION. Identical organisation membership does not make it Gen-1's frozen frame; Gen-1 is the committed bytes, not a recipe that may be re-cooked.
forwardRule.ifAFutureGenerationIsWanted: it is a NEW generationId with its own frame, its own frameHash and its own schema stamp, referencing this one by SHA-256 - never an edit.

immutability.thisRecordIsNeverEdited: A further adjudication is a NEW record that references this one by SHA-256.
